title: The first caliphates
blurb: Within a century, Muslim rule stretches from Spain to the Indus. Persia falls, Byzantium shrinks, the Quran is standardised.

events.title: Abu Bakr, first caliph
events.what: Abu Bakr is chosen as the first caliph. Tribes that renounce Islam or refuse zakat are brought back in the Ridda wars.
events.tie: Abu Bakr also had the Quran gathered into one written collection, after many of those who knew it by heart were killed at Yamama.

events.title: The Ridda wars
events.what: Tribes across Arabia refuse zakat or follow false prophets. Abu Bakr will not bargain: prayer and zakat stand together. Within a year Arabia is united again.
events.note: His words 'By Allah, I will fight whoever separates prayer from zakat' are reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim. Some early commentators read 5:54 as pointing to Abu Bakr and those who fought the apostates.

events.title: Musaylimah at Yamamah
events.what: Khalid defeats the false prophet Musaylimah in a walled orchard later called the Garden of Death. Hundreds of Muslims fall, many of them memorisers of the Quran.
events.note: Usually dated to late 11 AH (December 632). Wahshi, who had killed Hamzah at Uhud, is among those credited with killing Musaylimah.

events.title: The Quran is collected
events.what: Many memorisers die at Yamamah. Umar urges Abu Bakr to gather the Quran into one written copy. Zayd leads the work.

events.title: Khalid in Iraq
events.what: Khalid wins battle after battle against Persia in southern Iraq and al-Hira surrenders. Then he crosses the waterless Syrian desert to join the armies in Syria.

events.title: Umar ibn al-Khattab
events.what: Umar becomes caliph. He sets up the Hijri calendar, a treasury, stipends and courts across the new lands.
events.tie: Umar dated the calendar from the Hijra, so every Islamic date, including the AH years in this timeline, counts from the Prophet's ﷺ migration.

events.title: Damascus opens its gates
events.what: As news comes that Abu Bakr has died and Umar leads, the Muslims take Damascus. It surrenders on terms that protect its churches and people.
events.note: Some chroniclers date the surrender to 635 (14 AH). The city was briefly given up before Yarmuk and taken for good after it.

events.title: The Battle of Yarmuk
events.what: Khalid routs a far larger Byzantine army at the Yarmuk river. Syria is lost to Byzantium for good.

events.title: The Battle of Qadisiyyah
events.what: Sad defeats the Persian army at Qadisiyyah. The Sasanian capital Ctesiphon falls the next year.

events.title: Basra and Kufa
events.what: Basra and Kufa are founded as camp towns for the armies in Iraq. Within a century they are great cities of Quran reading, grammar and law.
events.tie: Most Muslims today recite the Quran in the reading of Asim of Kufa as passed on by Hafs, and Arabic grammar was first written down in Basra.
events.note: The founding dates vary in the sources between 635 and 638.

events.title: Umar enters Jerusalem
events.what: Jerusalem surrenders to Umar in person. Churches are protected by a written pact. He prays outside the church to keep it Christian.
events.tie: Al-Aqsa, the first qibla and the end of the Night Journey (17:1), came under Muslim rule, and Umar cleared its ground for prayer.

events.title: The plague of Amwas
events.what: Plague sweeps the army in Syria. Abu Ubaydah and Muadh ibn Jabal die with thousands. Umar, on his way north, turns back as the Prophet ﷺ taught.
events.note: The hadith 'If you hear of plague in a land, do not go there; if it breaks out where you are, do not flee' is reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

events.title: Egypt and Fustat
events.what: Amr takes Egypt from Byzantium and founds Fustat, the seed of Cairo, with the first mosque in Africa.
events.tie: The Prophet ﷺ told his companions to treat Egypt's people well, for they have protection and kinship, which scholars explain through Hajar and Mariya.

events.title: The end of Sasanian Persia
events.what: The last Persian army falls at Nahavand. The Sasanian empire, four centuries old, is finished.

events.title: Amr in Alexandria
events.what: Alexandria, Egypt's Greek capital, surrenders to Amr by treaty and the Byzantine garrison sails away. A Byzantine fleet retakes it in 645; Amr wins it back.
events.tie: Egypt, the land of Musa and Firaun in the Quran, becomes Muslim land and in time the home of al-Azhar.
events.note: The story that Amr burned the Library of Alexandria appears only centuries later. Most historians reject it.

events.title: Umar is martyred
events.what: Umar is stabbed while leading the dawn prayer. Dying, he names six Companions to choose the next caliph from among themselves. They choose Uthman.
events.note: His killer was Abu Lu'lu'ah, a Persian slave. Umar was buried beside the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr.

events.title: Japan's Taika reform
events.what: Japan's Taika reforms remake the islands into a Chinese-style state, with an emperor at the centre, written laws and land registers.
events.tie: In the same years Umar's diwan registered soldiers and stipends for the young Muslim state; Islam itself reached Japan only in modern times.

events.title: Umm Haram at sea
events.what: Muawiyah's first fleet sails to Cyprus. Umm Haram, whom the Prophet ﷺ foretold would sail with the first sea army, falls from her mount and dies there.
events.note: Her tomb, Hala Sultan Tekke near Larnaca, is still visited. Some date the expedition to 648.

events.title: Uthman's Quran
events.what: Caliph Uthman has master copies of the Quran made and sent to each province. Every Quran today follows this text.

events.title: An embassy to China
events.what: Envoys from the caliph reach the Tang emperor at Chang'an, the first Arab embassy in Chinese records. Muslim traders settle in Guangzhou and Quanzhou.
events.tie: China's oldest mosques, like Huaisheng in Guangzhou, grew from these trading communities.
events.note: Chinese Muslim tradition says Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas brought Islam to China; historians find no evidence that he went.

events.title: The Battle of the Masts
who: Abdullah ibn Sad ibn Abi Sarh
events.what: The young Muslim navy, its ships lashed together, defeats the Byzantine fleet of Emperor Constans II. Byzantium no longer rules the eastern sea alone.
events.note: Dated to 654 or 655 (34 or 35 AH).

events.title: Ali and the civil war
events.what: Uthman is killed by rebels. Ali becomes caliph and moves to Kufa. Civil war with Muawiyah follows at Siffin.
events.tie: Sunni Muslims honour Uthman and Ali alike as rightly guided caliphs, and count Ali, the Prophet's ﷺ cousin and son-in-law, as the fourth.

events.title: Uthman is martyred
events.what: Rebels from the provinces besiege Uthman in his house. He forbids the Companions to shed blood for him and is killed while reading the Quran.
events.note: The Prophet ﷺ gave Uthman glad tidings of Paradise along with a trial that would strike him (reported by al-Bukhari). Later reports say his blood fell on 2:137.

events.title: The Battle of the Camel
events.what: Aisha, Talhah and al-Zubayr come to Basra seeking justice for Uthman. Fighting breaks out with Ali's army. Afterwards Ali honours Aisha and sends her home.
events.note: Sunni scholars hold that both sides sought what they believed right and that the fighting began against the leaders' wishes. Scholars cite 49:9-10 on fighting between believers.

events.title: Siffin
events.what: Ali and Muawiyah's armies meet on the Euphrates. After weeks of fighting, copies of the Quran are raised on spears and both sides agree to arbitration.
events.note: Ammar ibn Yasir, son of Sumayyah, the first martyr, was killed here in his nineties.

events.title: The Khawarij at Nahrawan
events.what: Some of Ali's men reject the arbitration, crying that judgment belongs to Allah alone. They declare Muslims unbelievers and kill them. Ali defeats these Khawarij at Nahrawan.
events.note: The Prophet ﷺ spoke of people who recite the Quran but it does not pass their throats (al-Bukhari and Muslim). Scholars applied it to the Khawarij.

events.title: The Umayyads
events.what: Ali is assassinated. Muawiyah founds the Umayyad dynasty and rules from Damascus. The caliphate becomes hereditary.
events.tie: The Prophet ﷺ said the caliphate would last thirty years and then kingship would come; many scholars saw this fulfilled as the rightly guided era closed.

events.title: The Year of Unity
events.what: Hasan, Ali's son, gives up his claim to end the bloodshed. Muslims call it the Year of Unity.
events.tie: The Prophet ﷺ had said of Hasan: 'This son of mine is a sayyid, and perhaps Allah will make peace through him between two great groups of Muslims.'

events.title: Ali is martyred
events.what: Ibn Muljam, a Kharijite, strikes Ali with a poisoned sword at dawn prayer in Kufa. Ali dies two days later, the last of the four rightly guided caliphs.
events.note: Ali told his family to kill only his attacker, and only if he died.

events.title: Kairouan and the Atlantic
events.what: Uqba founds Kairouan, the base for Islam in North Africa. He later rides to the Atlantic.
events.tie: Kairouan's Great Mosque became a centre of Maliki law, where Sahnun taught the Mudawwana that spread across North Africa.

events.title: First siege of Constantinople
events.what: The first Muslim siege of Constantinople fails. Abu Ayyub, the Prophet's host in Madinah, is buried at its walls.

events.title: Karbala
events.what: Husayn, the Prophet's grandson, is killed with his family at Karbala by Yazid's army. Remembered every Ashura.

events.title: Srivijaya rules the straits
events.what: A stone inscription at Palembang records the rise of Srivijaya, a Buddhist sea power that controls the straits between India and China.
events.tie: These same sea lanes later carried Muslim traders, and Sumatra became home to Southeast Asia's first Muslim kingdom at Pasai.
events.note: The Kedukan Bukit inscription is dated 682.

events.title: The Dome of the Rock
events.what: Abd al-Malik builds the Dome of the Rock, the oldest surviving Islamic monument. Arabic becomes the language of state.
events.tie: It stands over the rock linked with the Prophet's ﷺ ascension, and its inscriptions quote the Quran on Isa as a messenger of Allah (4:171).

events.title: Coins of the Quran
events.what: Abd al-Malik strikes gold coins with no pictures, only words: Say, He is Allah, One. Arabic replaces Greek and Persian in the government offices.
events.tie: For the first time, verses of the Quran passed through every market and every hand in the empire.
events.note: The first all-Arabic dinar is dated 77 AH. The offices of Iraq and Syria switched to Arabic around 78 to 81 AH.

events.title: The Umayyad Mosque
events.what: Al-Walid I builds the Great Mosque of Damascus where a church once stood. Inside is a shrine said to hold the head of Yahya. One minaret bears the name of Isa.
events.tie: The Prophet ﷺ said Isa will descend by the white minaret east of Damascus; many link this to the mosque's eastern minaret.
events.note: The hadith does not name this mosque. The shrine of Yahya's head is a local tradition, not from the Quran or hadith.

events.title: Tariq crosses to Spain
events.what: Tariq crosses the strait that still bears his name and defeats the Visigoths. Muslim rule in Spain lasts 781 years.
events.tie: Al-Andalus gave Islam scholars like Ibn Hazm, Ibn Rushd and al-Qurtubi, whose tafsir is still read across the Muslim world.

events.title: Islam reaches the Indus
events.what: A seventeen-year-old general takes Sindh. Islam reaches the Indus.
events.tie: Muhammad ibn Qasim gave Sindh's Hindus and Buddhists protected status like the People of the Book, and Islam began its long story in South Asia.

events.title: Bukhara and Samarkand
events.what: Qutayba takes Bukhara and Samarkand. Central Asia, later home to al-Bukhari and Ibn Sina, joins the Muslim world.
events.tie: Samarkand later produced scholars like Abu Mansur al-Maturidi, whose theology most Hanafi Sunnis still follow.

events.title: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
events.what: Umar II rules for two years, returns wrongly taken wealth and ends abuses. Often called the fifth rightly guided caliph.
events.tie: He ordered the first official collection of hadith, writing to scholars like Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri to record the Prophet's ﷺ sunnah before it was lost.

events.title: The great siege of Constantinople
events.what: Maslamah leads a vast army and fleet against Constantinople. Greek fire, a bitter winter and the Bulgars break the siege, and Umar II calls the army home.
events.note: A hadith praising the army that conquers Constantinople is reported by Ahmad; some scholars grade it weak. The city fell to the Ottomans in 1453.

events.title: Write down the hadith
events.what: Fearing knowledge will die with the scholars, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz orders the hadith written down. Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri leads the first official collection.
events.note: His letter to Abu Bakr ibn Hazm is cited by al-Bukhari in the Book of Knowledge.

events.title: Covadonga
events.what: In the mountains of Asturias, the Visigoth noble Pelayo beats back a small Muslim force. A tiny Christian kingdom survives in the far north.
events.tie: Spanish tradition counts the long Reconquista from here; it ended with the fall of Granada in 1492.
events.note: Muslim chroniclers barely mention it, and the date may be 718 or 722.

events.title: The Battle of Tours
events.what: A Muslim raid from Spain is stopped near Tours by the Franks. The Pyrenees become the frontier.

events.title: The Abbasid revolution
events.what: The Abbasids, descendants of the Prophet's uncle, overthrow the Umayyads. One prince escapes to Spain.
events.tie: Descended from al-Abbas, the Prophet's ﷺ uncle, the Abbasids ruled in the name of his family, and their caliphate lasted, at least in name, until 1517.
